emerging_technology: Agentic AI built on large language models (LLM-based agents that plan, use tools, and complete multi-step tasks)
intended_application: Proposed bounded applicant-support workflow: retrieve approved program information, ask clarifying questions, plan next steps, and request a counselor appointment through a permission-limited tool. Staff approve outbound messages and any record changes. Excludes admission, scholarship, visa and eligibility decisions.
organization: Hypothetical small, tuition-dependent private liberal arts college (synthetic; not an observed institution)
industry_sector: Higher education - undergraduate and small graduate admissions. Peer group: small private colleges. Applicant trust, privacy and accessibility matter; exact legal obligations require specialist review.
business_need: Scenario hypothesis: reduce repetitive inquiry handling and improve timely guidance. Actual demand, response time and benefits have not been measured.
users_stakeholders: Prospective students, admissions counselors, marketing/enrollment staff, university IT and compliance officers
adoption_posture: Conservative / risk-averse: adopts only after peers demonstrate stable, low-risk use (scenario assumption).
capabilities_constraints: Scenario assumptions: two-person IT team, no in-house AI staff, limited budget, CRM vendor features only, small admissions office. No existing chatbot is specified.
risk_consequence_context: A visible error could damage the college's reputation in a small applicant market; unauthorized actions can expose data. No legal determination is made.
management_question: How far have agentic AI and agent-based applicant support diffused, what is accelerating or inhibiting that diffusion, and what timing implication follows for this college (without making the adoption decision)?
additional_context: Synthetic posture contrast. Technology and application held constant; posture, capabilities and peer group differ. General diffusion evidence should not move; the timing implication should.
